arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Fried argued the interest in IOLTA accounts is private property.
Mr. Fried argued the state took the property without just compensation.
Mr. Burman argued the plaintiffs' case has a fundamental flaw.
Mr. Dellinger argued a taking requires property, a taking, and denial of compensation.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether a state tax on interest from client trust accounts is a constitutional taking. the sides that brought the case argue the tax takes private property without just compensation. the opposing sides argue the tax is a valid exercise of state power.
